brief.subject: Bills due before payday? Ask to move the date
brief.headline: Shifting Bill Due Dates Can Ease Cash Crunch; FTC Sues to Block Playground Deal
brief.dek: Asking billers to change due dates may smooth cash flow, and the FTC moves to stop a playground equipment merger over price concerns.
brief.lede: If bills land before your paycheck does, asking billers to change your due dates is one way to ease the squeeze.

sections.heading: Line Up Due Dates With Payday
bullets: Billers can be asked to move your due date, a simple fix when payments hit before paychecks.
Matching due dates to payday can make monthly cash flow easier to manage.
This step targets timing, not the amount owed, so it helps most when money arrives a bit too late.

sections.heading: FTC Challenges Playground Equipment Merger
bullets: The FTC filed suit to stop PlayPower, owned by Platinum Equity, from acquiring rival BCI Burke.
The agency says the two firms are among the largest makers of commercial outdoor playground equipment.
Regulators argue the merger would weaken competition on price and quality in an already concentrated market.

brief.seo_description: Bills due before payday? Requesting new due dates can ease cash flow. Plus: the FTC sues to block a major playground equipment merger.
